question: At a dance party a group of boys and girls exchange dances as follows: one boy dances with \(5\) girls, a second boy dances with \(6\) girls, and so on, the last boy dancing with all the girls. If \(b\) represents the number of boys and \(g\) the number of girls, then:
solution:
The numbers of girls are \(5,6,7,\ldots\), increasing by one for each successive boy. From the first boy to the \(b\)-th boy there are \(b-1\) increases, so the last boy dances with
\[
5+(b-1)=b+4
\]
girls. He dances with all \(g\) girls, so \(g=b+4\). Therefore \(\boxed{b=g-4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
